prompt: Make Temperature a well-behaved member of the Java class hierarchy: implement compareTo and override equals, hashCode, and toString consistently. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Every class inherits equals, hashCode, and toString from java.lang.Object, and the default versions compare identity, not value -- which is why two separate Temperature(12) objects are unequal until you override them. The contract is strict: whenever equals says two objects match, hashCode MUST return the same number, or hash-based collections like HashSet will store duplicates. Implementing Comparable<Temperature> plugs the class into Collections.sort and TreeSet, and Integer.compare gives you the negative/zero/positive result those algorithms expect.
hints: equals should first check `o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()`, then cast and compare the celsius values.
Integer.compare(a, b) already returns a correct negative/zero/positive value -- do not subtract, which can overflow.
hashCode must agree with equals: derive it only from celsius, for example with Integer.hashCode(celsius).
